subject: Geopolitics
title: Quantum Computing and Cryptography
description: A quick win: understand Quantum Computing and Cryptography.

hook.text: A powerful quantum computer could break every encryption standard used today. Every secret becomes readable.

buildup.text: Current encryption relies on math problems too complex for classical computers. Quantum machines solve them differently.

discovery.text: Intelligence agencies are already collecting encrypted data they can't read yet — waiting for quantum to unlock it all.

twist.text: Post-quantum cryptography is being developed, but migrating the entire internet to new standards takes over a decade.

climax.text: The nation that achieves quantum supremacy first could read every rival's secrets before defenses catch up.

punchline.text: The lock you trust today may already have a future key.

quiz.question: Why are intelligence agencies collecting encrypted data they cannot yet read?
options: Current decryption methods will eventually improve naturally
Quantum computers may unlock the encryption in the future
Storage costs are declining making collection worthwhile
